title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
gist: Tests loops added to Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models after pretraining against two baselines: the same model trained identically without the loop, and the best unlooped use of the same inference compute. Loops are placed by calibrated perplexity on held-out text, never by benchmark answers. Training-free loops on released Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 32B are included, as are loops trained in with LoRA.
changes: Prices the compute a loop costs. A loop added after training paid only at 0.8B. On Qwen3-8B a training-free loop gained up to two points, not significantly, and a plain 14B beat it on MATH-500 at 1.3 times the time. Looping pays when weight memory binds, and time does not.
caveats: Two authors from one lab, with code promised only on acceptance. The benchmarks are mostly maths on reasoning models, so knowledge-heavy multiple choice, where the training-free paper found its gains, appears only as MMLU-Pro. The costliest 8B setting did help GSM8K and MMLU-Pro significantly, at 1.8 times the decoding time. Timing comes from one GPU at small batch.

bears_on.note: Loops added after training pay only under a fixed parameter budget; given more memory, a larger model is the better use of the compute.
